wave_4a_in_progress.adversarial_audit: AUDIT 2026-07-29, adversarial lens, run against cf46aab..b213668. FINDING: the tokenizer shipped in cf46aab was the right IDEA with the wrong MECHANISM, and it introduced a SECURITY REGRESSION. It deleted the contents of quoted spans; a shell does not delete quoted text, it strips the quote CHARACTERS and keeps the content as part of the surrounding word. So `git push "--force"` - an ordinary working command - became `git push ""` and was ALLOWED, while the old bare-regex guard had denied it. Probe result: 10 bypasses, 5 of them regressions versus the old guard (quoted long flag in either quote style, flag split by empty quotes, flag split mid-word, quoted short flag). The other 5 were pre-existing holes the old guard also missed (quoted subcommand, quoted command word, quoted db verb, quoted db middle word, quoted hard-reset flag). WHY THE CORPUS MISSED IT: all 18 rows quoted PROSE (a commit message, a grep pattern); not one quoted a FLAG. The 9 mutations were all aimed at the same assumption. A test suite cannot find a defect class it does not represent, and mutation testing only proves the rows respond to the mutations you thought of. FIX: shell-style word splitting - quotes contribute content and vanish as delimiters, adjacent segments join into one word - plus matching on word SEQUENCES rather than substrings, evaluated PER SEGMENT (split on ; && || | parens). Both properties then hold together: a quoted multi-word message cannot supply the adjacent words `git` `push`, while a quoted flag still is that word. Result: 0 bypasses, 0 regressions, and 4 cases now caught that the OLD guard also missed - strictly better than both prior implementations. The per-segment change also removed a false positive the first version had: `git reset --soft && tar --hard` no longer prompts. ALSO FOUND: two leftover has() calls in the DG_STRICT_GIT section referencing a helper the rewrite removed, which would have thrown at runtime. Reachable only with DG_STRICT_GIT=1, so the corpus (env unset) never executes that path - the ledger rows-5/6 test is what caught it. Concrete argument for testing the opt-in path.

non_blocking_unknowns.resolution: RESOLVED-NEGATIVE 2026-07-29 (PHV5-020), record CORRECTED after audit. The question cannot be answered locally: `claude plugin validate` does not read agent frontmatter at all. Falsifying control: `agents/risk-assessor.md` line 2 (`name: risk-assessor`) was deleted and `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json --strict` still printed 'Validation passed'; the directory form validates marketplace.json and likewise passed. `validate --help` confirms the scope: 'Validate a plugin or marketplace manifest'. TWO FURTHER PROBES WERE RUN AND BOTH PROVED NON-FALSIFYING, recorded so they are not mistaken for evidence: (a) `--agents` with tools ['Zzzdefinitelynotatool'] behaves identically to ['Read'] and ['Skill'], so the CLI does not validate tool names; (b) `claude --plugin-dir . plugin details deepgrade` does read the working tree but its 'Agents (22)' count tracks FILES, not parse success - a deleted `name:` line, invalid YAML, and an unterminated frontmatter block all still report 22; only removing the file drops it to 21. CORRECTION TO THE FIRST RECORD: it claimed `Skill` in `tools:` was 'spec-confirmed' while rejecting `skills:` as unverifiable. That was an asymmetric standard - validator silence is evidence about the validator, not about either mechanism - and the plan's own reference-data states the field exists ('plugin agent frontmatter supports a skills field to preload skills into subagents, plugins-reference, Agents section'). Both are spec-attested and neither is locally testable, so F27 now ships BOTH, needing only one to be honored. CONSEQUENCE BEYOND U1 (unchanged): the entire agent- and command-frontmatter defect class (F01, F02, F03, F07, F17, F21, F27) is invisible to `validate --strict`. U7 lists `validate --strict` among the EIGHT relied-upon behaviors - it is relied upon for manifest schema only, never component wiring. tests/layer1-config-wiring.sh is the sole guard for this class.

change_records.summary: ACCEPTED 2026-07-29 (owner: 'ratify CR-3'). Extends acceptance row A1 from *.sh to also cover *.js. G0 selected lane N, so the hook guards are node scripts, and .gitattributes stopped covering the files it exists to protect. SEVERITY REVISED UPWARD at ratification, against the proposal's own text: the falsifying control (clone HEAD with core.autocrlf=true) showed `file` reporting BOTH scripts/dg-git-guard.js and tests/codex-challenge-test.js as 'Node.js script executable ... with CRLF line terminators' while the .sh beside them stayed clean. The proposal said 'no known runtime failure' and rated this below CR-2; in fact the files carry a shebang and exec bit so direct POSIX execution fails with env: 'node', and codex-challenge-test.js runs Layer 5's 41 assertions - a third of the suite. Comparable to CR-2, not below it. What survives from the proposal: the shipped hook invocation (node scripts/dg-*.js) is unaffected because node tolerates CRLF. Guarded in layer1 section 14 via git check-attr (NOT git ls-files --eol, which reports w/lf with no .gitattributes at all and can never fail - the CR-2 lesson), with a derived-subject floor of 15 so a new script class cannot silently fall outside the policy, plus a check that the header rationale names both extensions. Only *.js added; *.py/*.ps1 stay uncovered because no tracked file uses them, and the floor is what surfaces the next class.

Owner ACCEPTED the weaker lane-N node-less signal (vendor hook-error notice instead of the round-4 friendly warning), conditional on U6 proving the notice's visible form. Raised by Codex round 8 GAP-5.

Supersedes acceptance-matrix row A1 on two points: (1) acceptance is the fresh-clone working-tree check - the git ls-files --eol clause reports w/lf for all 14 scripts with no .gitattributes present at all, so it is not falsifying; (2) scope extends from *.sh to also cover tests/fixtures/**, since layer3-fixture-lint.sh reads tab-separated fixture data where a trailing CR silently breaks every string comparison. Raised during Build Wave 0 by A1's own corrected falsifying test on first execution; clean clone showed Layer 3 at 7/2 vs 9/0 locally. The alternative - recording the two failures in expected-failures.txt - was rejected as enshrining a live defect, the R2 anti-pattern.
